context:
Goal: each iPhone or Mac app you ship gets a full test run with proof, without paying for one on every batch.
Problem (money): the full Swift suite needs a paid GitHub Mac machine, and how often it runs sets the cost, so it needs your word.
Based on (ruling): your Oct 27 ruling on CI: trust first, then cut in steps; the last step is full runs at milestones, after a set number of merges or a named milestone, not on every merge. It stays off in claude-settings because its minutes are free, and it carries to repos that pay for minutes.
Based on (ruling): a claude-settings rule wins over a repo's own rule unless the repo states an exemption; degen states none (searched Nov 1 18:35 CST).
Departs from: degen runs Swift only on your Mac, with no record — the full Swift suite runs on a GitHub Mac machine with a recorded result.

Your question: you are not misunderstanding. Your ruling is the second shape you named: merges keep landing with quick checks, and after a set number of them (or when you call a milestone) one full run tests main. No separate release branch is needed.

lastAnswer.note: i thought we agreed that most full scale tests are done not even at merge but at a milestone level? integration branches released at a milestone, or a full test after a set number of merges? or am i misunderstanding again

options.gain: Follows your Oct 27 ruling; Mac minutes only at milestones; proof at each one.
options.how: Batches merge on quick checks; after a set number of app batches, or when you call a milestone, one full Swift run on a GitHub Mac machine tests main, and a red run blocks the next merge until fixed.
options.label: Full Swift run at milestones
options.lose: A broken batch can sit on main until the next milestone run finds it.

options.how: Each app batch's checks run the full Swift suite on a GitHub Mac machine.
options.label: Full Swift run on every app batch
options.lose: The most Mac minutes, about 10 times the cost of Linux ones, on every batch.

options.how: degen records why it differs, and each batch posts the result of the run on your Mac for the merge to check.
options.label: degen states an exemption and keeps its Mac run
options.lose: An exemption to keep, and each batch waits on your Mac.

ref: step tci-5-platform-tested (each shipped platform names where it is tested)
reply: Withdrawn: your Oct 27 ruling already answers it. In repos that pay for minutes, the full run happens at milestones, after a set number of merges or when you call one, not on every batch. So degen's and mailaudit's full Swift suite runs at milestones on a GitHub Mac machine with a recorded result, and a red run blocks the next merge. degen states no exemption, so your shared rule applies there.
short: Proof of the batch app test
title: Your iPhone and Mac app tests run once per batch: should that run leave proof the merge can check?
why: It is the shape you already ruled for repos that pay for minutes, and it keeps Mac costs to milestones.
